content.text: The `cleaned_weekly_sales` table is the better choice due to its `calendar_year` and `week_number` columns, which simplify period-based calculations. I will define the four weeks before June 15th as weeks 20-23 and the four weeks after as weeks 24-27. I will now write a query to calculate the percentage change in sales for these periods in 2018, 2019, and 2020, grouping by year and using a `CASE` statement to distinguish between pre and post-June 15th sales.

args.sql:
WITH sales_periods AS (
    SELECT
        calendar_year,
        CASE
            WHEN week_number BETWEEN 20 AND 23 THEN 'before_june_15'
            WHEN week_number BETWEEN 24 AND 27 THEN 'after_june_15'
        END AS period,
        sales
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
    WHERE
        calendar_year IN (2018, 2019, 2020)
        AND week_number BETWEEN 20 AND 27
),
aggregated_sales AS (
    SELECT
        calendar_year,
        SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'before_june_15' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS before_june_15_sales,
        SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'after_june_15' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS after_june_15_sales
    FROM sales_periods
    GROUP BY
        calendar_year
)
SELECT
    calendar_year,
    (100.0 * (after_june_15_sales - before_june_15_sales) / before_june_15_sales) AS percentage_change
FROM aggregated_sales
ORDER BY
    calendar_year;

        calendar_year IN (2018, 2019, 2020)
        AND week_number BETWEEN 20 AND 27
),
aggregated_sales AS (
    SELECT
        calendar_year,
        SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'before_june_15' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS before_june_15_sales,
        SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'after_june_15' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS after_june_15_sales
    FROM sales_periods
    GROUP BY
        calendar_year
)
SELECT
    calendar_year,
    (100.0 * (after_june_15_sales - before_june_15_sales) / before_june_15_sales) AS percentage_change
FROM aggregated_sales
ORDER BY
    calendar_year;
